preamble: Debuccalization of the voiceless retroflex fricative [ʂ] to the glottal fricative [h]. It is found in Middle Indo-Aryan. In Pali and the Prakrits, Old Indo-Aryan ṣ before a nasal became h and moved after the nasal (ṣṇ > ṇh): Sanskrit tṛṣṇā > Pali taṇhā 'thirst'. Single intervocalic ṣ also appears as h in a few Prakrit words, e.g. Sanskrit pāṣāṇa 'stone' > Prakrit pāhāṇa, next to the regular reflex pāsāṇa.

examples.note: A variant pāsāṇa, with the regular s reflex, also exists.
ṣ before a nasal becomes h, which moves after the nasal; modern descendants include Hindi unāh and Marathi ūn.
ṣṇ > ṇh: the sibilant becomes h and moves after the nasal.
The ṣ before the nasal becomes h. The final ṣ, with no nasal after it, gives the regular Pali reflex s.
Oliveira (2014) gives h as the Poyanáwa reflex of *ʂ; most Panoan languages keep ʂ (Shipibo-Konibo ʂao).
